t: The first Contractors' All Risks policy is generally recognised to have been issued in 1929 for the construction of which structure?
o: Howrah Bridge, Calcutta
Sydney Harbour Bridge
Lambeth Bridge, London
Golden Gate Bridge, San Francisco
e: The CAR concept originated in the UK with the Lambeth Bridge project in 1929; the other bridges are not associated with the origin of CAR cover.

t: With effect from which date were engineering insurance premium rates in India freed from the Tariff Advisory Committee's tariff?
o: 1 January 2007
1 April 2005
1 April 2008
1 January 2010
e: IRDA de-tariffed fire, engineering and motor own-damage rates from 1 January 2007, while policy wordings continued to be regulated for some time.

t: Under a CAR policy, the sum insured for Section I (material damage) should represent:
o: The contractor's profit margin on the contract
The tender amount quoted by the lowest bidder
The principal's mobilisation advance to the contractor
The total value of the contract works on completion, including materials, wages, freight, customs duty and erection cost
e: CAR is written on a completed-value basis so that every item of work and material at risk during the contract is insured; profit margins or advances are not the measure of the exposure.

t: A CAR policy is issued for a 24-month highway project. Which of the following periods is NOT normally part of the policy period?
o: The construction period
The operational period after handing over to the principal
The testing period for plant items forming part of the works
The maintenance (defects liability) period, if opted
e: CAR cover ends on handover or first use of the works, whichever is earlier; operational risks thereafter fall under annual policies such as CECR or MBD.

t: A CAR policy carries an excess of 5% of the claim amount subject to a minimum of ₹25,000 for normal perils. Formwork collapses and the assessed loss is ₹3,60,000. The amount payable is:
e: 5% of ₹3,60,000 is ₹18,000, which is below the minimum of ₹25,000, so the excess deducted is ₹25,000 and ₹3,35,000 is payable.

t: Which CAR extension reimburses the cost of removing the debris of insured property damaged by an insured peril?
o: Clearance and removal of debris
Owner's surrounding property
Express freight
Escalation provision
e: Debris removal is a separate add-on with its own limit; surrounding property, express freight and escalation address different exposures.

t: Which of the following is NOT excluded under Section I of a standard CAR policy?
o: Loss discovered only at the time of taking an inventory
Damage caused by storm, flood and inundation
Wear and tear, corrosion, oxidation and deterioration
Penalties for delay, lack of performance or loss of contract
e: CAR is an all-risks cover and storm/flood are insured perils (subject to the AOG excess); inventory shortages, wear and tear and contractual penalties are standard exclusions.

t: The testing and commissioning period normally included in an Indian EAR policy without additional premium is:
o: 4 weeks
2 weeks
8 weeks
12 weeks
e: A standard testing period of four weeks is built into EAR cover; longer testing is granted at an additional premium.

t: Testing period cover under an EAR policy is excluded in respect of:
o: Imported machinery
Machinery erected by the owner's own staff
Second-hand or used machinery
Machinery valued above ₹1 crore
e: The testing of used machinery is excluded because the risk of hidden defects showing up during testing is too high to be covered at normal terms.

t: A Marine-cum-Erection (MCE) policy is generally preferred over separate marine cargo and erection policies because it:
o: Is always cheaper than the two policies combined
Covers consequential loss automatically
Is compulsory under IRDAI regulations for imported plant
Avoids disputes over whether damage occurred in transit or during erection, removing the need for the 50/50 clause
e: A single MCE policy has one insurer answering for transit, storage and erection; the 50/50 clause is needed only where marine and erection covers sit with different insurers.

t: Under the Insurance Act, 1938, the provisions on surveyors and loss assessors are contained in Section:
o: 64VB
64UM
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 64UM deals with licensing of surveyors and the requirement of survey reports; 64VB is premium in advance, 45 non-contestability and 41 rebating.

t: An EAR policy is issued with a sum insured of ₹40 crore at a rate of 0.30% for the full project period. The premium before GST is:
e: ₹40,00,00,000 × 0.30% = ₹12,00,000; GST at 18% would be added on this amount.

t: Which of the following forms part of the sum insured of the plant under an EAR policy?
o: The owner's loss of production during erection
Freight and customs duty paid on the plant
The contractor's profit on the erection contract
Interest on project loans
e: The EAR sum insured is the completed erected value, including freight, customs duty and erection cost; production loss and interest are ALOP subjects, not material damage.

t: Which of the following is specifically excluded under a standard EAR policy?
o: Fire and explosion occurring during erection
Theft of insured items from the project site
Damage due to carelessness of the erection crew
Loss or damage due to faulty design
e: EAR covers accidental physical loss including fire, theft and negligence of workmen; faulty design (for the defective part) is a standard exclusion.

t: Under a CPM policy, the sum insured for each machine should be:
o: Its book value as per the balance sheet
Its original purchase price less depreciation
The current replacement value of a new machine of the same kind and capacity, including freight and duties
The hire charges payable for the project period
e: CPM is written on new replacement value so that partial losses can be repaired without underinsurance; book value or hire charges do not reflect the exposure.

t: A CPM policy covers the insured machinery:
o: While at work, at rest, or being dismantled and re-erected for cleaning or overhaul at the site
Only while actually at work on the site
Only while in transit between two sites
Only during the hours of the contractor's shift
e: CPM responds whether the plant is working or idle on site; transit between sites is covered only when the transit extension is bought.

t: Which of the following is normally excluded under a CPM policy?
o: Fire damage to a dumper on site
Collision of a crane with a structure
Overturning of an excavator on a slope
Electrical or mechanical breakdown of the machine
e: CPM covers external accidental damage; internal breakdown is excluded and falls under an MBD policy.

t: A Machinery Breakdown policy indemnifies loss arising from:
o: Fire, lightning and explosion in the plant
Theft and burglary of machinery
Sudden and unforeseen physical loss caused by mechanical or electrical breakdown of the insured machinery
Flood and inundation of the factory
e: MBD responds to internal causes such as defects, short circuit, misalignment or operator error; fire, theft and flood are fire-policy perils and are excluded.

t: A medical centre insures a CT scanner under EEI for ₹3 crore. A total loss occurs when the actual value (replacement less depreciation) is ₹2.1 crore and the new replacement cost is ₹3 crore. Ignoring excess and salvage, the insurer pays:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Total losses under EEI are settled at actual value; the new replacement sum insured governs partial losses and underinsurance only.

t: Which of the following causes is covered under a standard MBD policy?
o: Corrosion, erosion and rust
Short circuit and excess voltage
Chemical explosion
Deliberate overloading during an experiment
e: Electrical causes such as short circuit are classic MBD perils; corrosion, chemical explosion and overloading/experiments are excluded.

t: A compressor insured under MBD for ₹8 lakh suffers a total loss. Its new replacement value at the time of loss is ₹10 lakh and depreciation works out to 30%. Ignoring excess and salvage, the insurer pays:
e: Total loss is settled at actual value (₹10 lakh less 30% = ₹7 lakh); as the sum insured is only 80% of the replacement value, average reduces this to ₹5,60,000.

t: Which item is NOT covered under MBD, being a specifically excluded replaceable part?
o: Belts, ropes, wires and fuses
Gear box of a crusher
Rotor of a turbine
Stator winding of a motor
e: Consumable and quickly wearing parts such as belts, ropes, fuses, dies and refractory linings are excluded; main structural components are covered.

t: Under an MBD policy a partial loss is settled on the basis of:
o: Cost of repair less depreciation on the whole machine
Actual value of the machine immediately before the loss
Cost of repairs necessary to restore the machine to its former working condition, without depreciation on replaced parts
Market value of an equivalent second-hand machine
e: Partial losses are paid on repair cost without depreciation; depreciation is applied only in a total loss or on parts with limited life.

t: Under a Boiler and Pressure Plant policy, 'explosion' is defined as:
o: Ignition of accumulated flue gases in the furnace
Sudden and violent rending of the boiler or pressure plant by force of internal steam or fluid pressure, causing bodily displacement with forcible ejection of contents
Gradual bulging of a plate due to overheating
Failure of an individual tube in a water-tube boiler
e: The policy definition requires rending by internal pressure (other than pressure of ignition or chemical action); flue gas explosion is a fire-policy peril and tube failure is excluded.

t: A cold storage insures potatoes under DOS with sum insured ₹2 crore. The insured compressor breaks down and 20% of a stock valued at ₹1.5 crore deteriorates; salvage realised is ₹5 lakh. Ignoring excess, the claim is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Loss = 20% × ₹1.5 crore = ₹30 lakh, less salvage of ₹5 lakh = ₹25 lakh; no average applies as the stock value is within the sum insured.

t: Which of the following is covered under a BPP policy?
o: Loss of profit due to shut-down of the boiler
Flue gas explosion in the furnace
Legal liability for third-party bodily injury or property damage caused by explosion or collapse of the insured plant
Damage to the boiler by fire in the boiler house
e: BPP covers damage to the plant, damage to the insured's surrounding property and third-party liability arising from explosion or collapse; fire and flue-gas explosion are fire-policy perils.

t: Statutory inspection and certification of boilers in India is governed by:
o: The Boilers Act, 1923
The Factories Act, 1948 only
The Explosives Act, 1884
The Electricity Act, 2003
e: The Boilers Act, 1923 and the Indian Boiler Regulations, 1950 govern registration and periodic inspection of boilers by the State Boiler Inspectorate.

t: Section II of an Electronic Equipment Insurance policy covers:
o: Material damage to the insured equipment
Increased cost of working
External data media and the cost of reconstructing the data stored on them
Third-party liability
e: EEI has three sections: I material damage, II external data media, and III increased cost of working; there is no liability section.

t: The sum insured under Section I of an EEI policy should be:
o: Written-down value as per the books of account
Replacement value of equipment of the same kind and capacity, including freight, duty and installation
Original invoice value only
Market value of a used equipment of similar age
e: EEI is written on new replacement value to avoid underinsurance on partial losses, which are paid without depreciation.

t: Which loss is excluded under Section I of an EEI policy?
o: Theft of a server from the insured premises
Scratches on painted or polished surfaces (aesthetic defects)
Damage to a CT scanner by a short circuit
Fire damage to a telephone exchange
e: Aesthetic defects that do not affect functioning are excluded; theft, electrical causes and fire are all insured perils under EEI.

t: Under Section III (Increased Cost of Working) of an EEI policy, the insurer pays:
o: Profits lost due to equipment downtime
Cost of upgrading to newer equipment
Salaries of idle operators
Additional expenditure for hiring substitute equipment to continue data processing after insured damage
e: ICOW cover reimburses extra costs of substitute facilities for an agreed indemnity period; it does not pay lost profit or betterment.

t: A Deterioration of Stock policy is normally issued only if:
o: The cold storage building is less than 5 years old
The stock is also insured under a marine cargo policy
The refrigeration plant is insured under an MBD policy with the same insurer
The insured holds a valid FSSAI licence
e: DOS is a consequential cover riding on the MBD policy of the refrigeration machinery; the machinery policy is a precondition.

t: Deterioration of stock due to accidental failure of the public electricity supply is:
o: Available as an extension at an additional premium
Covered under the basic DOS policy
Not insurable in India
Covered only under a fire policy
e: Power-supply failure is an add-on to DOS; load-shedding and deliberate withholding of supply by the authority remain excluded.

t: Which of the following is excluded under a DOS policy?
o: Deterioration due to rise in temperature following breakdown of the insured compressor
Deterioration due to escape of refrigerant from the plant
Shrinkage, inherent defects or diseases of the stock
Deterioration due to sudden failure of the insured condenser
e: Inherent vice, shrinkage and disease are excluded as they are not caused by the insured machinery; breakdown of the plant and escape of refrigerant are covered.

t: A Civil Engineering Completed Risks policy is designed for:
o: Civil works still under construction
Completed civil engineering structures such as dams, bridges, roads and tunnels, on an annual basis
Contractors' plant lying at the site
Electronic equipment in a control room
e: CECR takes over after the CAR period ends and protects completed structures against named perils during operation.

t: The CECR policy is written on which basis?
o: Named perils basis
All risks basis
Loss of profit basis
Legal liability basis
e: Unlike CAR, CECR covers only listed perils such as fire, earthquake, flood, storm, impact, landslide and riot.

t: Under Section 45 of the Insurance Act 1938, a life insurance policy cannot be called in question on any ground after how many years from the date of issue, revival or rider addition, whichever is later?
o: Two years
Three years
Five years
One year
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The 2015 amendment made the three-year bar absolute: after three years no policy may be questioned on any ground, including fraud.

topic: Advance Loss of Profits (ALOP) and Machinery Loss of Profits (MLOP)
t: An Advance Loss of Profit (ALOP/DSU) policy can be taken by:
o: The contractor only
Any sub-contractor on the project
The principal or owner of the project only
The project financier only
e: Only the principal has an insurable interest in the profit from the completed project; the contractor's exposure is penalty, which is excluded.

topic: Advance Loss of Profits (ALOP) and Machinery Loss of Profits (MLOP)
t: The loss indemnified under an ALOP policy is:
o: Financial loss due to delay in commencement of commercial operation caused by material damage indemnifiable under the CAR/EAR policy
Cost of repairing the damaged works
Penalties payable by the contractor for delay
Increased cost of construction due to inflation
e: ALOP responds only to delay flowing from an insured material-damage event; delays from other causes are not covered.

topic: Advance Loss of Profits (ALOP) and Machinery Loss of Profits (MLOP)
t: The 'time excess' in an ALOP or MLOP policy means:
o: The maximum indemnity period under the policy
The time limit for submitting a claim
The period after which the policy lapses
The number of days or weeks of delay or interruption borne by the insured before indemnity begins
e: The time excess is the deductible expressed in time; it is applied at the start of each interruption.

topic: Advance Loss of Profits (ALOP) and Machinery Loss of Profits (MLOP)
t: Under an MLOP policy the annual gross profit is ₹2.4 crore, the indemnity period 12 months and the time excess 14 days. A covered breakdown stops production for 44 days. Ignoring savings, the loss payable is approximately:
o: ₹28.9 lakh
₹9.2 lakh
₹19.7 lakh
₹24.0 lakh
e: Only 30 days (44 less the 14-day time excess) are indemnifiable; ₹2.4 crore ÷ 365 × 30 ≈ ₹19.7 lakh.

topic: Advance Loss of Profits (ALOP) and Machinery Loss of Profits (MLOP)
t: An MLOP policy is granted only when:
o: A fire loss of profit policy exists
An MBD or BPP policy on the same machinery is in force
A CAR policy exists for the plant
The machinery is less than five years old
e: MLOP is a consequential cover that follows admissible material damage under MBD/BPP; the material damage policy is a precondition.

t: Section 41 of the Insurance Act 1938 prohibits:
o: Assignment of a life policy
Payment of any rebate of premium or commission as an inducement to buy insurance
Nomination by a minor
Issue of a policy without a medical examination
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 41 bars rebating; contravention attracts a penalty of up to ₹10 lakh.

t: For engineering underwriting, the seismic zoning map of India (IS 1893) divides the country into zones:
o: I to III
I to IV
A to D
II to V
e: IS 1893 currently classifies India into seismic zones II to V, zone V being the most severe; zone I has been merged with zone II.

t: While underwriting a CAR proposal for a bridge, the most relevant document for assessing the time-wise build-up of values at risk is:
o: The contractor's balance sheet
The construction bar chart or schedule
The pollution clearance certificate
The list of site employees
e: The bar chart shows the sequence and timing of works, enabling the underwriter to judge peak exposure and the testing period.

t: Which factor would most increase the risk under an EAR policy for a thermal power project?
o: Erection carried out by the manufacturer's own engineers
Location in seismic zone II
An extended hot testing period of 12 weeks
A short period of storage at site
e: Testing, especially hot testing, is the most hazardous phase of erection; manufacturer supervision and low seismic zone reduce risk.

t: Section 64VB of the Insurance Act, 1938 requires that:
o: No risk be assumed unless the premium is received in advance or guaranteed as prescribed
A licensed surveyor assess every engineering claim
All engineering risks be reinsured with GIC Re
Every policy be registered with IRDAI
e: Section 64VB is the 'premium in advance' rule; it is why cover under CAR/EAR starts only after premium or instalment is received.

t: Under IRDAI regulations, a licensed surveyor and loss assessor must be appointed for a non-motor claim exceeding:
e: The IRDAI surveyor regulations fix ₹50,000 for motor claims and ₹1,00,000 for claims other than motor as the threshold for compulsory survey.

t: In the event of a loss under a CAR or EAR policy, besides immediate notice, the insured must submit the claim in writing within:
o: 7 days
14 days
30 days
60 days
e: The claims condition requires immediate intimation and a written claim with particulars within 14 days so that the insurer can arrange a survey.

t: After paying a CAR claim for damage to the works caused by a negligent sub-contractor's crane operator, the insurer recovers from the sub-contractor. This is an application of the principle of:
o: Contribution
Indemnity
Subrogation
Proximate cause
e: Subrogation gives the insurer the insured's rights of recovery against a third party after indemnity; contribution operates between insurers.
